para: The four edge types are not mutually exclusive at the level of pairs of calculi; a single pair may be related by more than one edge of different types, and identifying such coincidences is itself a source of structural information about the graph. What distinguishes the graph from an untyped Hasse diagram is precisely the differentiation of edge types: it is possible, and important, to know not merely that two calculi stand in some relation but which relation or relations hold between them and in which direction. An extension edge is directed from the weaker to the stronger calculus; an embedding edge is directed from the source to its host; a duality edge is directed according to the convention established in the construction of , where the notion of a primary and derived calculus within a dual pair will be made precise. Equivalence edges are undirected.
